proof_summary: The tenth substitution iterate has length at most \(4^{10}=1{,}048{,}576\), and all later proxy values default to nonzero, so there are too few zero positions; consequently the occurrence search defining \(a(1{,}048{,}577)\) falls back to index \(0\), giving \(a(1{,}048{,}577)=1\). Since \(\sqrt3\ge0\), the resulting discrepancy at this index is already greater than \(2\), providing the counterexample.
